sources.cite: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide (PDF): Design Secure Architectures 30%, Design Resilient Architectures 26%, Design High-Performing Architectures 24%, Design Cost-Optimized Architectures 20%

Quoted: Task 2.1 'Determining the AWS services required to achieve loose coupling based on requirements', Task 3.2 'Decoupling workloads so that components can scale independently'; Task 1.3 'Encrypting data at rest (for example, AWS KMS)', 'Implementing access policies for encryption keys'; Task 2.2 'Service quotas and throttling', Task 4.4 'Selecting an appropriate throttling strategy'.

sources.cite: AWS Big Data Blog, 'Detect and handle data skew on AWS Glue'
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: 'You can use the Spark UI to identify which tasks are taking longer to complete than others'; with skew 'you will see very biased values in each percentile'; the observability metrics glue.driver.skewness.job and glue.driver.skewness.stage; a job that 'doesn't scale with the number of workers' is a symptom; Glue 4.0 (Spark 3.3) enables Adaptive Query Execution by default; salting 'involves adding a random prefix to the key of skewed data'. Splitting out a placeholder key before a join is the author's applied example (general Spark practice, to verify against the Spark tuning guide).
